title: The most terrifying words Jesus ever spoke were not directed at atheists.
paragraphs: The most terrifying words Jesus ever spoke were not directed at atheists.
They were spoken to religious people.
People who believed they were safe.
People who believed they were saved.
People who believed they belonged to Him.
In Matthew 7:23, Jesus gives one of the most sobering warnings in all of Scripture:
“Then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness.’”
Pause for a moment and let that sink in.
These are not people who openly rejected God.
They are people who thought they were serving Him.
Just a few verses earlier, Jesus describes them saying:
“Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name?”
“Did we not cast out demons in Your name?”
“Did we not perform many mighty works in Your name?”
They were doing religious things.
They were using the name of Jesus.
They were active.
They were visible.
They probably looked like powerful believers to everyone around them.
But Jesus exposes the one thing that truly matters.
He does not say:
“I knew you once but you fell away.”
He says something far more chilling.
“I never knew you.”
Not once.
Not ever.
This passage reveals something deeply uncomfortable for many people.
Christianity is not merely about activity.
It is not about public displays of spirituality.
It is not about titles, ministries, influence, or religious reputation.
It is about relationship.
You can know the language of Christianity and still not know Christ.
You can attend church for years and still not know Him.
You can preach sermons, sing worship songs, lead Bible studies, or serve in ministry and still miss the one thing that matters most.
Knowing Jesus is not about outward performance.
It is about a transformed heart.
A real relationship with Christ produces real obedience.
Jesus even says earlier in the same passage:

“Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of My Father who is in heaven.”
(Matthew 7:21)
That statement alone should cause every believer to pause and examine their heart.
Because Jesus is warning us about something very dangerous:
False assurance.
The kind of assurance that says:
“I prayed a prayer once, so I’m fine.”
“I go to church, so I’m fine.”
“I believe in God, so I’m fine.”
But the real question Jesus asks is not:
Did you attend church?
Did you say the right words?
Did you look religious?
The real question is:
Did you truly know Me?
And the evidence of knowing Christ is not perfection.
It is transformation.
When someone truly encounters Jesus, their life begins to change.
Sin is no longer something they casually embrace.
Their heart begins to desire righteousness.
They grow in repentance.
They grow in humility.
They grow in obedience.
They grow in love for God.
Not because they are trying to earn salvation.
But because they have encountered the Savior.
Jesus is not impressed by religious performance.
He sees the heart.
He knows what is genuine.
And He knows what is fake.
This warning from Matthew 7 is not meant to create panic.
It is meant to wake people up.
Because the door of salvation is still open.
Grace is still available.
Mercy is still extended.
Jesus is still calling people to Himself.
But the invitation is not to simply admire Him from a distance.
It is not to use His name while living for ourselves.
It is to follow Him.
To surrender.
To repent.
To walk with Him daily.
The greatest tragedy is not rejection by the world.
The greatest tragedy would be to spend your entire life believing you belong to Christ…
only to hear Him say:
“I never knew you.”
So the real question today is not:
“Do you know about Jesus?”
The real question is:
Does Jesus know you?
Engagement Question

If Jesus asked you today, “Why should you enter My kingdom?”
What would your answer be?
